researched_writeups.title: Vistry Group (VTY.LN)
researched_writeups.summary: Presents Vistry Group's pivot from a traditional, capital-intensive homebuilder into the UK's leading pure-play 'partnerships' affordable housing provider . By pre-selling over 50% of homes to cycle-agnostic local authorities and housing associations, the model significantly shortens cash conversion cycles, mitigates interest rate and housing market risk, and structurally raises return on capital employed (ROCE).

researched_writeups.title: [Free] Vistry: Breaking the (Land)Bank
researched_writeups.summary: Analyzes Vistry's transition into a high-velocity, capital-light partnerships model characterized by negative incremental capital requirements. By unwinding its massive legacy landbank, management plans to release ~£1 billion in cash (roughly 50% of its market capitalization) to supercharge share repurchases at substantial discounts to tangible net asset value.

researched_writeups.title: The Vistry Mystery | A Special Situation
researched_writeups.summary: Evaluates whether Vistry can replicate NVR's asset-light, capital-efficient business model in the UK market following a sharp sell-off caused by regional cost overruns. The author argues that short-term issues in legacy housebuilding operations conceal a resilient partnerships engine trading at sub-8x P/E and a deep discount to book value.

researched_writeups.title: Tell me why Vistry Group (VTY) isn't deep value
researched_writeups.summary: Frames Vistry Group as a classic Benjamin Graham asset-play opportunity trading at a ~57% discount to tangible net asset value (£2.3B+ TNAV vs £1B market cap). The thesis examines downside protection provided by physical land and work-in-progress inventory alongside operational catalysts including balance sheet deleveraging and net cash targets as legacy homebuilding unwinds.
